attempts.summary: Established an AIDE-based file integrity baseline for /etc on node1 (RHEL 7.9). Installed aide 0.15.1 from CentOS vault (no subscription-manager repos were enabled), configured /etc/aide.conf to scope FULL (permissions/inode/owner/group/size/mtime/ctime/acl/selinux/xattrs/md5+sha256) monitoring to /etc, initialized and activated the baseline database at /var/lib/aide/aide.db.gz, added a weekly cron job (/etc/cron.d/aide-check) for ongoing checks, and validated detection works via a reversible add/remove test. Completed the mandatory restart protocol: captured boot_id baseline, triggered a native reboot, confirmed boot_id changed, verified the AIDE database and config survived and correctly detected a legitimate post-boot change (/etc/resolv.conf regenerated by DHCP), then refreshed the baseline to the current clean state (final check: 'All files match AIDE database. Looks okay!').
